## Setting
Deciding what the break room is for. A shared room next to a small office has been used for several purposes at once, and it can no longer serve all of them. The five people who use it are settling its use. Participants: Shunichi, May, Servas, Ryuji and Jonathan. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Invoices for outside hire by the hour
- Quotes for the two fit-outs
- Facilities callouts on this floor
- Round trip for a hot lunch
- The partition wall to the office
- Crumbs and bins at the desks
- Fortnight's tally of use by person
- Final clear-out of the old fridge
- Unplanned talk since the refit
- Where the last awkward conversation happened

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Jonathan, May, Shunichi and Servas. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Shunichi
Age: 32
Gender: male
Personality: Shunichi is a very confident person who can remain calm in any situation. He is not modest, and has a slightly sarcastic side, but that is part of his charm. He is not sociable, but he is good at communicating at the right time and is relied upon by those around him. He rarely becomes overly emotional and can analyze situations calmly and act accordingly, so he has an unexpectedly rational side.
Concern: Whatever we settle on, somebody has to sign for it, and we are already paying out month by month because that room will not do the one thing we keep needing it for. I would rather see the figures on paper before we agree to anything.

Name: May
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. She understands her own appeal well and knows how to behave appropriately in different situations. She can be a little challenging and sometimes comes across as cold, but she basically has a charisma that attracts people.
Concern: Every arrangement this building has tried ends up eating somebody's hours, either in upkeep that nobody actually volunteered for or in the walking about it leaves the rest of us doing. Before we commit to anything I want to know where those hours really go.

Name: Servas
Age: 85
Gender: male
Personality: Servas has a very calm and composed personality. Based on the knowledge and experience he has gained over the years, he often gives advice to those around him. He is an excellent listener and can talk openly with anyone. He also occasionally expresses deep philosophical thoughts, and his words inspire many people. He is full of vitality and always gives positive energy to those around him.
Concern: I sit two metres from that door all day, and so does everyone else, and what happens in there does not stay in there. The complaints I hear are never about principle; they are about sound and mess, so I went and looked at both.

Name: Ryuji
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.
Concern: Nobody ever decided how that room gets used; it simply goes to whoever gets there first, and the clearing up afterwards lands on whoever minds the most. I did not want to argue about any of that from impressions alone.

Name: Jonathan
Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.
Concern: We work a few metres apart and have somehow ended up strangers to one another, and when something difficult does need saying there is nowhere to say it. Whatever we choose has to be judged on that as much as on the fittings.

## Hidden information

Options (see the schedule above):
- A: Open Kitchen. The room is fitted out for preparing and eating food, with the appliances and storage maintained by whoever uses them.
- B: Quiet Room. The room is kept for individual rest with conversation and calls taken elsewhere, and the furniture is arranged for people sitting alone.
- C: Meeting Space. The room becomes bookable for small discussions, with a table and a screen installed and a shared calendar governing its use.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Invoices for outside hire by the hour: Last year's invoices show 68,000 yen paid to the hourly room-hire place on the main road, across nine bookings, none of which was for more than four people.
- Quotes for the two fit-outs: The quotes came back at 141,000 yen for a screen, bracket, cabling and a table to match, and 96,000 for a hob, fridge and the extra circuit an electrician must run.
- Facilities callouts on this floor: Facilities logged eleven callouts last year across the two rooms on this floor that hold equipment, and none for the store room that was emptied, which has only chairs in it.
- Round trip for a hot lunch: The round trip to the nearest counter selling a hot lunch takes twenty-five minutes once the queue is counted, and most of the office makes it three or four days a week.
- The partition wall to the office: The wall to the office is a single sheet of plasterboard; from the desk nearest it, a listener could follow both halves of a phone call held inside with the door shut.
- Crumbs and bins at the desks: Three of the five keyboards in the office have crumbs under the keys, and the desk bins have been going out daily since people started eating where they sit.
- Fortnight's tally of use by person: A fortnight's tally shows the two people sitting nearest the door had the room eleven times between them, and everyone else four times in total.
- Final clear-out of the old fridge: When the fridge in the old back room was emptied out for good, half of what came out belonged to nobody, and the same person had done the clearing twice before.
- Unplanned talk since the refit: Since the corridor sofa went in the refit, the only unplanned talk left happens by the printer, and the two who started in spring still barely know the rest of the office.
- Where the last awkward conversation happened: The last awkward thing that had to be said between two colleagues was said across the desks in front of everyone, and the pair went quiet for a fortnight.

On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.
